title: Fix Node.js pipe buffer hang — read stdout/stderr pipes
description:
**Source:** Internal audit Sprint 60 (2026-07-11) finding P0-004

`MinecraftAdapter.cs` (line ~93) starts the Node.js process but never reads its `stdout` or `stderr` pipes. If the adapter writes enough stdout/stderr output (e.g., console.log from Mineflayer, structured logging), the OS pipe buffer fills up (typically 64KB on Windows, 16KB on Linux/macOS). When full, the Node.js process blocks on `write(2)` — it stops making progress until the pipe is drained. This effectively hangs the adapter.

**Impact:** Under verbose logging or error conditions, the adapter will appear to hang. The C# side sees a healthy process (no crash) but the adapter stops processing commands.

**Recommendation:** Add asynchronous pipe readers for both stdout and stderr. The simplest approach: redirect stdout/stderr to the same logger used by the adapter, or use `Process.BeginOutputReadLine()`/`BeginErrorReadLine()`. For production, consider using a pipe draining strategy (discard after a buffer limit) to prevent blocking.
